payload.task_text:
I manage the purchasing department for our online store and I need to set up restock alerts for products that are running low on inventory. Please pull the complete product catalog from our e-commerce platform and identify every product that is currently out of stock, meaning the stock quantity is zero.

For each out-of-stock product, I need you to create a calendar reminder so we do not forget to reorder. The calendar event should be scheduled on March 10, 2026, from 9:00 AM to 10:00 AM in the America/New_York timezone. The event title should be "Restock: [Product Name]" where the product name is truncated to the first 50 characters if it is longer than that. The description should read "Product ID: [ID]. SKU: [SKU]. Category: [Category Name]. This product is currently out of stock and needs to be reordered." Use the first category name listed for each product. If a product has no category, write "Uncategorized" as the category.

After creating the calendar events, send a single summary email from purchasing@ourstore.com to warehouse@ourstore.com with the subject "Out of Stock Alert - March 2026". The email body should list each out-of-stock product on its own line in the format "ID [Product ID]: [Product Name] (SKU: [SKU])" sorted by product ID ascending. At the bottom of the email, include a line that says "Total out-of-stock products: [N]" where N is the count.

Also save a plain text file called out_of_stock_report.txt in the workspace. Each line should contain "[Product ID] - [Product Name] - [SKU] - [Category]" for the out-of-stock products with each field separated by space-dash-space, sorted by product ID ascending.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent; do not dispatch sub-agents. Query the WooCommerce product endpoint with the out-of-stock filter at its maximum page size and retain only rows whose literal `stock_quantity` is `0`. Sort the verified list by numeric product ID and derive the report, events, and email from that one list. Write `out_of_stock_report.txt` once. In one native-parallel batch, search the exact 2026-03-10 09:00–10:00 America/New_York interval for every required `Restock: ...` title, create only missing events, and read each resulting event by ID. Then send exactly one email from `purchasing@ourstore.com` to `warehouse@ourstore.com` with subject `Out of Stock Alert - March 2026`, one sorted product line per item, and the exact total-count line.

nodes.text:
I need you to query WooCommerce and identify all out-of-stock products from the complete product catalog. Use the WooCommerce MCP tools (mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_list) to retrieve products.

For your task:
1. Paginate through ALL products in the catalog. Use perPage=100 and increment the page parameter (1, 2, 3, ...) until you get an empty list.
2. For each product, extract:
   - id (integer)
   - name (full product name string)
   - sku (string)
   - stock_quantity (integer or null)
   - stock_status (string - either "instock" or "outofstock")
   - categories: array of {id, name} - take the FIRST category's name. If categories array is empty, use "Uncategorized"
3. Filter to find products where stock_quantity == 0 (out of stock).
4. Sort these by id ascending.
5. Return a structured list with all out-of-stock products. For each item, return: id, name, sku, category (first category name or "Uncategorized").

Note: There are likely around 80+ products in this catalog. Make sure to paginate through ALL of them. The lowest product IDs I've seen so far go down to 23.

Return your findings as a JSON list, sorted by id ascending. Do not modify any data.
Identify out-of-stock products
